answer: Escrow makes a sybil swarm expensive. Each agent identity must lock a bonded stake to act, so one operator spinning up a thousand fake peers has to fund a thousand real deposits, and that capital stays frozen until settlement. Every withdrawal becomes a visible bridge between accounts that auditors trace and slash on a shared ledger. Reputation already earned is a relic that dies when an account is cloned or dumped. Graders consult an atlas of cross-linked records, so correlated accounts surface as one cluster.
